articles.title: George Street Roadworks Scheduled for 1 October 2026 in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: George Street will be temporarily closed for roadworks on 1 October 2026, affecting traffic flow and access to nearby streets.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that part of George Street will be temporarily closed on Thursday, 1 October 2026, from midnight until 11.59pm. The closure will extend 20 metres south of the junction with Ramsay Street and end 20 metres north of the same junction.

During this period, no waiting will be permitted in the closed section of the road. The roadworks are expected to impact traffic flow, particularly affecting access to nearby streets including Entwisle Road, Nile Street, Ramsay Street, Kitchen Street, and Norreys Street.

Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes during the roadworks. The council has provided a map of the roadworks and other restrictions across Greater Manchester for those wishing to navigate around the affected area.

Further information regarding the roadworks can be found on the Rochdale Borough Council website, where updates will be posted as the date approaches.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches Good Food Strategy to Enhance Local Food Access
articles.excerpt: The Good Food Strategy aims to improve access to healthy and sustainable food across Rochdale, involving residents and businesses in its implementation.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched its Good Food Strategy, which aims to ensure that healthy, affordable, and sustainable food is accessible to all residents. The strategy outlines collaboration with community groups, businesses, and partners to enhance food availability in the borough.

Key actions include increasing access to nutritious food, building food skills and confidence among residents, and strengthening local food networks. The initiative also seeks to celebrate Rochdale's diverse food culture.

This strategy reflects the council's commitment to addressing food insecurity and promoting healthier eating habits. Residents and local businesses are encouraged to participate in the strategy's implementation.

Further details can be found on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

The portal, described as 'Rochdale's Media Portal for a New Generation and the 21st Century', focuses on delivering news and media content that reflects the interests and needs of residents.

articles.title: Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield to Receive £20 Million for Community Improvements
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale council is set to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising the historically overlooked areas of Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield, with plans to improve local facilities and services.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield are set to benefit from nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising these historically overlooked areas. The Rochdale council is expected to accept the Pride in Place funding at a town hall meeting on August 25, which will provide a total of £19.6 million over the next decade, equating to just under £2 million annually.

The funding aims to address various local needs, with early suggestions including tackling congestion, improving parking, creating new green spaces, enhancing local facilities, and expanding maternity services. However, no specific plan has yet been established for how the funds will be allocated. The council will also approve the formation of the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board, which will be responsible for developing proposals for the funding. This board will consist of local community figures, including MP Paul Waugh and council regeneration officer Coun Daniel Meredith, and will be chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group.

The Neighbourhood Board has until November 30, 2026, to submit a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government to unlock the funding. Initial government support of £150,000 has already been granted to establish the board and generate the plan. Local residents have expressed skepticism about the funding, citing a history of neglect and lack of investment in their communities. Ken Whittle, a local resident, noted that the area has been left looking tired and unloved, while another resident, Dinah Banks, emphasised the need for better healthcare services.

Rochdale MP Paul Waugh has been actively engaging with the community to gather input on their needs and priorities. Once the council formally accepts the funding and the Neighbourhood Board is established, local views will play a crucial role in shaping the future development of these areas.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Step-free access is available via alternative routes until further notice.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 8:09pm on 18 August 2026, impacting passengers using the tram service. There is currently no confirmed date for when the lift will be restored.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are encouraged to check the latest travel alerts on the Transport for Greater Manchester website for ongoing updates regarding the lift's status and any other travel disruptions.

Further information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website, where live travel alerts are regularly updated.

articles.title: Rochdale to Hold Farewell Event for Comedian Jimmy Cricket
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to beloved comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a public viewing and funeral services next week.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to pay tribute to legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket, who died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. Known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', Cricket was a prominent figure in the comedy scene during the 1970s and was a dedicated supporter of local charities.

His body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale on Thursday, August 20, from 3pm to 5pm, allowing fans and friends to pay their respects. Following this, a vigil mass will take place at Salford Cathedral at 7pm, marking the reception of his body.

The funeral service will be held at Salford Cathedral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, a nod to Cricket's trademark style, which also included his iconic Wellington boots.

Jimmy Cricket's contributions to comedy and his local community have left a lasting impact, and his passing is felt deeply by those who knew him and appreciated his work. The public events provide a chance for the community to come together to celebrate his life and legacy.

articles.title: Pakistan Threatens to Halt Acceptance of Illegal Migrants Over Rochdale Rapist Deportation
articles.excerpt: Pakistan has issued a warning to the UK, stating it will stop accepting illegal migrants if the deportation of a convicted rapist from Rochdale goes ahead. This situation raises concerns about future deportations and immigration policies.
articles.content_html:
Pakistan has warned the United Kingdom that it will cease accepting illegal migrants if the UK proceeds with the deportation of a man convicted of rape in Rochdale.

The warning comes amid ongoing discussions about the deportation of individuals with criminal convictions, with the Pakistani government expressing strong opposition to such actions.

This development could have significant implications for the UK's immigration policy and its ability to manage deportations effectively.

The UK government has not yet responded to Pakistan's threat regarding the deportation.
